The equation is homogeneous. Put $y=vx$, so $dy=v\,dx+x\,dv$.
$x\sin v\,(v\,dx+x\,dv)=(vx\sin v-x)\,dx \Rightarrow x^2\sin v\,dv=-x\,dx$
Separate the variables: $\sin v\,dv=-\dfrac{dx}{x}$
Integrate: $-\cos v=-\ln x+C \Rightarrow \cos v=\ln x+C_1$
Apply $y(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, i.e. $v=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ at $x=1$: $0=0+C_1$, so $C_1=0$ and $\cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)=\ln x$
So $\alpha=\cos\left(\dfrac{y(e^{12})}{e^{12}}\right)=\ln e^{12}=12$
The circle is $x^2+y^2-2px+2py+14=0$, with centre $(p,-p)$ and $r^2=2p^2-14$
Conditions: $r^2>0 \Rightarrow p^2>7$ and $r\le 6 \Rightarrow 2p^2-14\le 36 \Rightarrow p^2\le 25$
Integer solutions: $p=\pm3,\pm4,\pm5$, which is 6 values
Answer: 6

Rewrite: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}-\dfrac{1}{\sin(y/x)}$ (homogeneous); put $y=vx$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$.
$v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=v-\dfrac{1}{\sin v}\Rightarrow \sin v\,dv=-\dfrac{dx}{x}$.
Integrate: $-\cos v=-\ln x+C\Rightarrow \cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)=\ln x-C$.
At $x=1$, $v=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$: $0=0-C\Rightarrow C=0$, so $\cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)=\ln x$.
$\alpha=\cos\left(\dfrac{y(e^{12})}{e^{12}}\right)=\ln e^{12}=12$ (formal value; a cosine cannot really be 12, but the question intends this).
Circle: $x^2+y^2-2px+2py+14=0$, centre $(p,-p)$, $r^2=2p^2-14$.
Real circle: $2p^2-14>0\Rightarrow p^2>7$; $r\le 6$: $2p^2-14\le 36\Rightarrow p^2\le 25$.
$7<p^2\le 25\Rightarrow p=\pm3,\pm4,\pm5$; a point circle would need $p^2=7$, which has no integer solution.
Answer: 6
